parts.name: body shell

physics.Basic_description: Dark grey metallic frame forming the head and structural backbone of the wrench, with a matte finish.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the rigid structure holding the fixed jaw and guiding the movable jaw mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper can grasp the flat sides of the head or the neck area near the handle to apply torque.
physics.reason: The head contains a slot for the movable jaw and worm screw, implying internal voids, though the walls are thick cast metal.

parts.description: Dark grey metallic frame forming the head and structural backbone of the wrench, with a matte finish.
parts.function: Provides the rigid structure holding the fixed jaw and guiding the movable jaw mechanism.

parts.name: wood grip

physics.Basic_description: Brown, turned wooden handle with a smooth finish, cylindrical shape tapering slightly at the ends.
physics.Functional_description: Provides a comfortable, insulated grip for the user to apply force without slipping.
physics.Grasped_description: The primary grasp target; a parallel jaw gripper would close around the cylindrical mid-section.
physics.reason: Traditional tool handles of this type are solid wood dowels or turnings for strength.

parts.description: Brown, turned wooden handle with a smooth finish, cylindrical shape tapering slightly at the ends.
parts.function: Provides a comfortable, insulated grip for the user to apply force without slipping.

parts.name: ferrule collar

physics.Basic_description: Small gold-colored metallic ring located where the wooden handle meets the metal head.
physics.Functional_description: Reinforces the wood against splitting and secures the handle to the metal tang.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and flush to be a primary grasp point; would be covered by the hand or gripper jaws.
physics.reason: Small reinforcing collar, effectively solid or thick-walled relative to its size.

parts.description: Small gold-colored metallic ring located where the wooden handle meets the metal head.
parts.function: Reinforces the wood against splitting and secures the handle to the metal tang.

parts.name: butt cap

physics.Basic_description: Dark grey metallic cap at the very end of the handle, featuring a hexagonal hole.
physics.Functional_description: Protects the handle end and may serve as a nut driver or hanging point.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped from the end, but offers poor leverage for wrenching; usually avoided.
physics.reason: Contains a hexagonal socket hole, indicating it is a cup-shaped or hollowed component.

parts.description: Dark grey metallic cap at the very end of the handle, featuring a hexagonal hole.
parts.function: Protects the handle end and may serve as a nut driver or hanging point.

parts.name: jaw shell

physics.Basic_description: Dark grey metallic sliding block with a flat gripping face, positioned within the wrench head.
physics.Functional_description: Slides along the track to adjust the jaw width for different nut/bolt sizes.
physics.Grasped_description: Could be grasped to manually adjust position, but not suitable for applying main wrenching torque.
physics.reason: Movable jaws are typically forged solid steel blocks to withstand high compressive loads.

parts.description: Dark grey metallic sliding block with a flat gripping face, positioned within the wrench head.
parts.function: Slides along the track to adjust the jaw width for different nut/bolt sizes.

parts.name: worm wheel

physics.Basic_description: Small knurled metallic wheel visible on the side of the wrench head.
physics.Functional_description: Rotated by the thumb to drive the screw mechanism that moves the adjustable jaw.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small for a standard gripper to manipulate effectively; requires fine motor skills.
physics.reason: Small gear/wheel component, effectively solid metal.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
